stem: A logistics company must choose transfer approaches for two different needs: moving a one-time 200 TB archive from a data center with no viable network bandwidth for the transfer, and separately ingesting a continuous stream of GPS pings from delivery trucks into the data lake. Which TWO approaches fit these two needs respectively? (Select TWO.)

choices.text: The physical AWS Data Transfer Terminal facility for the offline archive
An AWS DataSync task for the offline archive
An S3 File Gateway for the continuous GPS stream
An Amazon EMR cluster for the continuous GPS stream
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams for the continuous GPS stream

rationale: With no viable network path for a 200 TB transfer, AWS now directs customers to the physical AWS Data Transfer Terminal facility for a large offline transfer, since Snowball Edge devices are no longer available to new customers. Kinesis Data Streams is built to continuously ingest a stream of small telemetry records like GPS pings at whatever ordered, replayable throughput the fleet needs. AWS DataSync moves data online over the network; with no viable network bandwidth for a transfer this size, DataSync is not a fit, which is exactly why AWS points to the physical Data Transfer Terminal facility instead. An S3 File Gateway presents a persistent file share for an application that reads and writes files, not a target for a continuous stream of individual location events. An EMR cluster processes data already sitting in storage; it isn't an ingestion path for a live stream.
